title: Orchestration Cue Cards & Checkpoints — May 2026 (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working set of short, actionable "cue cards" and a lightweight calendar covering a staged rollout for the 2026-05 feature bundle (runtime kernel swaps + batching changes + API schema minor). Goal: give on-call, release lead, and SRE a single-page set of checklists to run a low-friction rollout, plus a companion draft of customer-facing release notes.

Status & assumptions:
- Draft; intended for run-through on 2026-05-05 staging rehearsal.
- Assumes release window 2026-05-09 02:00–08:00 UTC (EMEA-friendly).
- Canary traffic via weighted routing (alpha=1%, beta=10%, gamma=50%).
- Telemetry hooks (sampling) already instrumented — see linked artifacts.

High-level rollout sequence (quick):
1) Preflight (T-72h to T-2h): sanity checks, DB schema confirmed, migration dry-run done.
2) Staging rehearsal (T-48h): full automated smoke + manual verified endpoints.
3) Canary alpha (T+0): 1% traffic for 30m -> metrics check -> if green move to beta.
4) Canary beta: 10% for 60m -> metrics check & error sampling -> if green move to gamma.
5) Gamma: 50% for 45m -> final checks -> traffic to 100% over 15m ramp.
6) Post-launch monitoring (T+0 to T+6h): increased sampling, error triage channel open.

Windows and regional notes:
- North America peak avoidance window: 14:00–18:00 PT (avoid changes).
- EMEA midday preferred.
- No deploys to US-west early: use staggered regional ramp if anomalous.

Preflight checklist (must be green before starting):
- [ ] Release branch built and SHA pinned in release manifest (release-manifest v2).
- [ ] All required PRs merged + deployment tags set in GitHub. PRs: see linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Migration plan reviewed; dry-run OK in staging DB.
- [ ] Canary routing policy created + reviewed by networking.
- [ ] Ops runbook updated (this doc snapshot saved to confluence).
- [ ] Pager rota and escalation list confirmed; on-call present for entire window.
- [ ] Post-deploy rollback artifacts ready (helm chart previous tag, rollback job script).

Alpha (1%) cue card — quick steps:
- Update routing weight to 1% for new variant via rollout API.
- Start 30-minute timer.
- Notify #release-ops: "alpha started — sha=<SHA>".
- Watch critical signals every 5m: 5xx rate, median latency (p95), token-per-request cost delta, queue length on workers.
- If any of the stop conditions occur, immediately flip weights back to 0% and escalate to SRE lead.

Beta (10%) cue card — quick steps:
- If alpha green, update weight to 10% and start 60-minute timer.
- Enable expanded sampling: store full request+response sample for 0.1% of requests for manual QA.
- Coordinate with Customer Success for any customers on dedicated capacity (heads up only).
- Run smoke regression subset of eval prompts (list in linked artifacts).

Gamma (50%) cue card — quick steps:
- Ramp to 50% in controlled steps: 20% -> 35% -> 50% with 5–10 minute stabilization windows.
- Start end-to-end business checks: billing events, function calling latency, streaming session success rate.
- Prepare staged full cutover plan: if green, trigger 100% ramp over 15 minutes.

Stop / rollback conditions (examples — be conservative):
- Sustained increase in 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 3 consecutive 5m windows.
- P95 latency increase > 250ms absolute over baseline for 10m.
- Token cost per request > 20% above expected soft limit for 30m.
- RPS surge causing queue depth increase > 2x baseline for 15m with queue growth trend.
- Any customer-facing data corruption or failed migrations observed.

Rollback quick plan:
- Immediate: set new variant weight to 0% and restore previous routing.
- Run rollback smoke tests (endpoints + critical flows).
- Collect triage bundle: logs (last 30m), heap/dump traces, sample requests. Attach to incident.
- If rollback fails to restore health, open incident commander (IC) and escalate to platform-eng manager.

Observation & telemetry queries (notes):
- Critical dashboards: API 5xx rate, p95 latency per model, KV cache hit rate, GPU job queue depth, new-kernel error logs.
- Suggested sampling increments: alpha=0.01, beta=0.1, gamma=0.5 (percent of traffic).
- Quick log grep pattern: "runtime:error|kernel:invalid-alloc|kvcache:miss*" — add to ops deck.

Communication templates (quick copy):
- Slack status: "[RELEASE] alpha START — sha=<SHA> — monitoring 30m — ping @oncall"
- Customer note (CS stub): "We are rolling an infrastructure update with staged canary. Short interruptions unlikely, CS will reach out if we see anomalies."

Draft release notes (customer-facing, short):
Title: May 2026 performance and reliability update
Summary: This release includes a set of runtime improvements to reduce token latency and lower unit cost for short-sequence workloads. We also expanded batching heuristics and fixed an intermittent KV-cache issue that caused higher tails for some models.
Highlights:
- Optimized attention kernel selection to reduce median token latency by up to 8% on common sequences.
- Improved automatic batching heuristics to reduce per-token compute for bursty traffic.
- Resolved an intermittent KV-cache expiry bug that could increase p95 for multi-turn chats.
Notes for integrators:
- API is backward compatible; no schema changes that require action.
- If you use private deployments, coordinate with your solutions engineer for staging rollout.

Unresolved / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm whether billing/invoice event hooks need sampling changes.
- Get sign-off from privacy/compliance on the sampling policy for request recording.
- Add explicit list of eval prompts to linked artifacts (Riley to upload).
- Rehearse rollback once in staging with simulated failures (Liam).

Appendix: quick contacts
- Release lead: Ava Martinez (pager: ava-release, slack: @avam)
- SRE on-call: Noah Patel (pager: noah-sre)
- Platform eng backup: Liam Chen (slack: @liamc)
- Customer Success triage: Riley Gomez (slack: @riley)

---
Notes: Keep this doc intentionally terse — the single-page cue cards should be copied into the runbook template before finalizing. After rehearsal, we convert to the formal runbook and attach rehearsal logs.
